_what_this_is: Item 6. One hand-written judgment per UNGUARDED retryable write that somebody has actually READ. tools/idempotency_check.py reports a shape; this records what was decided about it and why. A file with no entry here is UNTRIAGED, and the checker counts those separately -- which is the whole point, because 'being triaged' with no denominator is indistinguishable from nothing happening.

_verdicts.SAFE: a retry cannot duplicate the effect, and the reason is stated. No work.
_verdicts.FIX: a retry duplicates a real effect. Names the consequence and the pattern to copy.
_verdicts.ACCEPTED: a retry DOES duplicate something, and duplicating it is correct or harmless. The reason is the important half -- an accepted finding with no reason is an ignored one.
_verdicts.FIXED: a FIX that has been BUILT. Kept as its own verdict rather than deleted: an entry that vanishes on being fixed leaves nobody able to tell a defect that was closed from one nobody ever judged.

_not_a_blanket_sweep: Every entry below was reached by reading the write, its schema and its error handling. TWENTY-FIVE files of twenty-nine are judged. The remaining two -- api/sc-credentials.js and api/sd-webauthn.js, both credential inserts -- are named by the checker as UNTRIAGED and are NOT covered by any statement here. They are unread, not cleared.

api/agent/stripe-webhook.js.why: The only write is setPlanStatus(), a PATCH of plan_status to a CONSTANT string -- 'paid' or 'canceled'. An absolute assignment, not an increment and not an append, so replaying the same webhook writes the same value. Stripe retries webhooks by design and this survives it.
api/agent/stripe-webhook.js.but: A DIFFERENT defect lives here and idempotency guards would not fix it: Stripe does not guarantee delivery ORDER. If subscription.updated->canceled is delivered before a delayed invoice.paid, the agent flips back to 'paid' after being cancelled. That is an out-of-order hazard, not a retry hazard, and it is recorded here so it is not lost -- it needs an event-timestamp comparison, not a dedupe key.

api/sairncash/trial-start.js.why: The row cannot duplicate -- sql/sairncash_trial_schema.sql:18 makes email UNIQUE, so a retry gets a 409 and the handler answers ALREADY_EXISTS explicitly. So it is idempotent against duplicate ROWS.
api/sairncash/trial-start.js.but: It is NOT idempotent against duplicate REQUESTS, and that is the real defect. trialToken is minted per request and returned ONLY on the 200 path. If the insert commits and the response is lost -- a client timeout, a dropped connection -- the retry gets 409 and the caller NEVER RECEIVES THE TOKEN THAT WAS MINTED. The trial exists and is unreachable. The handler's own message anticipates it: 'Contact support if you need help accessing it.'
api/sairncash/trial-start.js.fix: Copy api/sairndental/public-complaint-submit.js, which solved exactly this a day earlier: on the duplicate branch, SELECT the existing row and return the ORIGINAL answer rather than an error. A user who retried must see their trial, not a support instruction.
api/sairncash/trial-start.js.fixed: 2026-09-14. An OPTIONAL client-supplied idempotency_key, stored as a sha256; a retry carrying the same key gets the ORIGINAL token back. NOT the 'return the existing token on 409' fix public-complaint-submit.js uses -- that would be a CREDENTIAL DISCLOSURE here, because this endpoint is public, Access-Control-Allow-Origin *, and its only input is an email address. api/sairncash/trial-start.test.js section C is the arm for that: right email plus wrong key must still get ALREADY_EXISTS. Needs sql/sairncash_trial_idempotency_2026-09-14.sql.

api/agent/enqueue.js.why: Inserts a row into sairn_agent_commands with no key, no unique constraint and no read-before-write. A retry after a lost response enqueues a SECOND command, and an agent polling the queue executes it a second time. This is the plainest real instance of the shape in the whole list: the effect duplicated is an arbitrary agent OPERATION, not a log line.
api/agent/enqueue.js.fix: A caller-supplied idempotency key carried on the row with a unique index on (agent_id, idempotency_key), and the enqueue returning the existing command_id when it collides. Note that the current response already returns command_id, so the shape of the fix is the same as trial-start's: return the original answer, do not error.
api/agent/enqueue.js.fixed: 2026-09-14. An OPTIONAL idempotency_key with a PARTIAL UNIQUE index on (agent_id, idempotency_key); a retry carrying the same key returns the ORIGINAL command_id instead of queueing a second command. Not hashed, unlike trial-start's, and the migration says why: that key retrieves a credential and this one retrieves nothing. A failed read-back tells the caller the command IS queued and NOT to retry with a new key -- being told only 'try again' is what would make them queue it twice. Needs sql/sairn_agent_commands_idempotency_2026-09-14.sql.

api/_lib/audit.js.why: writeAuditLog() appends a row, so a retry appends a second. That is correct and must not be guarded. An audit log records what was ATTEMPTED; if a caller really did retry, two attempts happened and two rows is the truthful record. Collapsing them on a dedupe key would HIDE a real double-execution, which is the opposite of what this table is for.
api/_lib/audit.js.but: The duplicate row is a SYMPTOM of the caller's retry, not the disease. Where a duplicated audit line appears, read the write it was auditing -- that is where the finding is.

api/sairndental/public-complaint-submit..why: NOT UNGUARDED AND NEVER WAS -- this was a checker false negative, corrected 2026-09-14. It hashes a submission_key over license_hash + NUL + patient name + NUL + message, reads it back with a ten-minute window before writing, and returns the ORIGINAL complaint's answer on a duplicate. It has its own migration, sql/sairndental_complaint_idempotency_2026-09-13.sql. It read as UNGUARDED only because 'submission_key' was not in idempotency_check.py's hand-written key vocabulary.
api/sairndental/public-complaint-submit..but: It is now the SECOND real positive fixture in that checker's blind lock, so the term cannot be dropped and the guard go invisible again. api/ledger.js alone could not have caught this: it uses two terms the list already knew.

api/cron-watchdog.js.why: The POST is to Resend: it SENDS AN ALERT EMAIL. A retry sends it twice. Same judgment and same reasoning as api/alf-alerts.js -- a duplicated alert is noise, and SUPPRESSING a repeat alert is the more dangerous failure for a watchdog whose whole job is to be noticed.
api/cron-watchdog.js.but: Two files now reach this verdict for the same reason. If duplicate alerts ever become the complaint, Resend's Idempotency-Key header fixes both together -- and they should be fixed together, because a fix applied to one is a fix somebody will believe covers the other.

api/_lib/auth.js.why: NOT A DATABASE WRITE. The only POST is oidcExchangeCode() posting an authorization code to the identity provider's token endpoint. A retry re-presents the code, and an authorization code is single-use BY THE IdP -- OAuth 2.0 requires it to be rejected on reuse. Nothing of ours is duplicated because nothing of ours is written.
api/_lib/auth.js.but: THIS IS A SCOPE LIMIT OF THE CHECKER, not a property of this file. idempotency_check.py counts ANY POST/PATCH/PUT as a mutating fetch, so every outbound call to a third party reads as an unguarded write. Expect more of these in the untriaged remainder and judge them on whether OUR store changes, not on the verb.

api/provisioner-health.js.why: A HEALTH PROBE THAT CANNOT WRITE, deliberately. It calls the rate limit RPC with p_app_id: '' -- and sql/sairn_ai_rate_limit_consume_fn.sql returns {error: 'app_id required'} on an empty app_id BEFORE taking the advisory lock and before the insert. Confirmed by reading the function, not inferred from the endpoint's name. The probe exercises reachability and records no usage, so a retry records nothing twice.
api/provisioner-health.js.but: It depends on a refusal in a DIFFERENT file staying where it is. If that early return ever moves below the insert, this health probe starts writing rate-limit rows on every run and nothing here would say so.

api/network.js.why: Appends a row to network_insights. A retry appends a second, so the duplicate is real -- and what duplicates is one advisory insight in a list a human reads. No money, no identity, no count computed from it, and nothing downstream acts on the row automatically.
api/network.js.but: ACCEPTED IS NOT SAFE and the difference is the point: this one does duplicate. It is accepted because the consequence is a repeated line on a screen. If anything ever computes a total from this table, or triggers on a row, re-read this entry -- the judgment is about the consequence and the consequence would have changed.

api/org-intel.js.why: Same shape and same reasoning as api/network.js: an append to sairnscape_org_intel of one text insight, read by a human, with nothing computing a total from it or triggering on it. A retry shows the insight twice.
api/org-intel.js.but: Same conditional as network.js. Two files reaching the same verdict for the same reason is worth noting rather than collapsing -- if the reason turns out wrong it is wrong in both, and a single merged entry would hide the second one.

api/_lib/courtlistener.js.why: The write is an RPC call to cl_rate_limit_consume, which does the count and the insert in ONE transaction under pg_advisory_xact_lock (sql/cl_rate_limit_consume_fn_2026-09-04.sql:96). There is no gap between reading the count and recording the use, so there is nothing for a retry to race.
api/_lib/courtlistener.js.but: This is the FIXED one of the four rate limiters on this platform, and reading it is what showed two others were not. See the wex and intl-caselaw entries.

api/_lib/wex.js.why: COUNT-THEN-INSERT, THE ITEM 78 RACE, IN A SECOND PLACE. checkLimit reads wex_rate_limit_log filtered on requested_at in one HTTP call, decides, then POSTs a row in another. Nothing coordinates them -- verbatim the shape docs/spec/RateLimitConsume.tla models and tools/rate_limit_race_model.js proves violates the cap. N concurrent lookups all see an empty window and all proceed.
api/_lib/wex.js.consequence: This limit is not ours to overspend: it honours Cornell LII's PUBLISHED Crawl-delay. Over-running it hammers a third party's server and risks the IP being blocked, which would take the feature down for every customer. Bounded by requests in flight, like the AI one -- racy is not unbounded.
api/_lib/wex.js.fix: The pattern is already written TWICE here: sql/cl_rate_limit_consume_fn_2026-09-04.sql and sql/sairn_ai_rate_limit_consume_fn.sql. Re-qualify rather than copy byte-for-byte (disciplines item 7): the wex limit is a CRAWL-DELAY, at most one row in the window, not an N-per-day cap.

api/_lib/intl-caselaw.js.why: THE SAME RACE, THIRD PLACE. checkLimit(table, seconds, max) reads the count, compares it to max, then POSTs. Two HTTP calls with nothing between them. It is the GENERIC form of the wex one -- it serves more than one ledger table -- so one fix here covers every source it limits.
api/_lib/intl-caselaw.js.consequence: Same class as wex: these limits exist to honour other people's published rates, so over-running them is a politeness and access failure rather than a money one, and the cost lands on every customer if the source blocks us.

api/_lib/ai-rate-limit.js.why: The racy count-then-insert is the FALLBACK path, taken whenever the atomic RPC is unavailable. The file is honest about it -- it reports mode observe-racy / enforce-racy precisely so the race is visible in the return value.
api/_lib/ai-rate-limit.js.but: WHETHER THE FALLBACK IS LIVE IS NOT KNOWABLE FROM THIS REPO. db/schema_snapshot.json carries TABLES ONLY and has never held a function, so the earlier 'verified NEVER RUN' claim was not supportable in either direction. Read the mode the endpoint returns. Nothing to build here beyond running the migration.

api/claude.js.why: NOT A WRITE TO OUR STORE. The POST is to api.anthropic.com -- this file IS the proxy Guardian check 1 requires every call to go through. A retry duplicates no record.
api/claude.js.but: It duplicates a BILLED API CALL and consumes rate-limit budget, which is a real cost consequence even though it is not a data-integrity one. Named rather than folded into SAFE silently.

api/sc-eligibility.js.why: The POST is an eligibility INQUIRY to Stedi, a third party. Nothing of ours is written by it and the upstream effect is a read.
api/sc-eligibility.js.but: Clearinghouse transactions are typically billed per inquiry, so a retry costs money without duplicating data. Same shape as claude.js.

api/agent/poll.js.why: Two PATCHes, both filtered by PRIMARY KEY and both ABSOLUTE assignments: a last_seen_at timestamp on sairn_agents and a status change on one command row. A retry writes the same shape of value to the same row. No increment, no append.

api/agent/register.js.why: PATCH sairn_agents by id with status active and a last_seen_at. An absolute assignment by primary key; replay is a no-op.

api/agent/result.js.why: PATCH sairn_agent_commands by id with a status, a result and a completed_at, all derived from THIS request's body. A retry of the same request writes the same values to the same row.
api/agent/result.js.but: It is absolute, not conditional -- a LATER result for the same command_id overwrites an earlier one. That is a different question from idempotency (which result is authoritative) and is not a finding here; named so the next reader does not re-derive it.

api/sairncash/trial-renew.js.why: A READ-MODIFY-WRITE ON A COUNTER, and the sharpest thing in this batch. It SELECTs renewal_count, computes plus one in JavaScript, then PATCHes that value back along with a fresh expires_at computed from NOW.
api/sairncash/trial-renew.js.consequence: TWO failures, both real. (1) LOST UPDATE: two concurrent renewals both read N and both write N+1, so one renewal vanishes from the count. (2) DOUBLE EXTENSION ON RETRY, which is worse: if the PATCH commits and the response is lost, the retry reads N+1, writes N+2 AND a new expires_at 30 days from the retry -- the trial is extended twice from ONE admin approval. This endpoint is admin-approval-gated, so that is an entitlement granted beyond what was approved.
api/sairncash/trial-renew.js.fix: Two halves, because one does not cover the other. A compare-and-set (renewal_count=eq.N in the PATCH filter) closes the lost update: the loser gets zero rows back and knows. An idempotency key closes the double extension, the same shape trial-start now uses -- a retry returns the ORIGINAL expiry instead of computing a new one.
api/sairncash/trial-renew.js.fixed: 2026-09-14, and it needed BOTH halves because neither covers the other. A COMPARE-AND-SET (`renewal_count=eq.<N>` in the PATCH filter, or `is.null` for an untouched row) closes the lost update: the loser matches zero rows and is told, as a 409 CONCURRENT_RENEWAL rather than a silent success -- PostgREST returns 200 with an EMPTY ARRAY to the loser, so a handler checking only `ok` would report a renewal that never happened, and the PATCH asks for return=representation because `minimal` returns no body to count. An OPTIONAL idempotency key closes the double extension: a retry carrying the same key gets the ORIGINAL expiry back and writes nothing. Needs sql/sairncash_trial_renew_idempotency_2026-09-14.sql. Three sabotages verified: dropping the retry recognition, dropping the CAS filter, and ignoring the zero-row result each take arms red.

api/sairncash/trial-verify.js.why: One best-effort PATCH of a constant status, filtered by trial_token. An absolute assignment, and the file already says a failure here does not change the answer it computed. Replay writes the same value.

api/_lib/employee-lifecycle.js.why: PATCH of an active flag and updated_at, scoped to one employee in one licence. The flag is derived from the REQUEST, not toggled from the stored value, so a retry sets the same state. A TOGGLE here would be the classic version of this bug and it is not one.

api/alf-alerts.js.why: The POST is to Resend: it SENDS AN EMAIL. A retry sends it twice, which is a real duplicate side effect even though nothing of ours is written. Accepted because a duplicated ALERT is noise -- the recipient sees the same warning twice -- and suppressing a repeat alert is the more dangerous failure in a care setting.
api/alf-alerts.js.but: Resend supports an Idempotency-Key header, so the fix is cheap if duplicate alerts ever become the complaint. Recorded so that is a decision rather than a rediscovery.

api/audit-checkpoint.js.why: The append cannot duplicate: sql/audit_checkpoint_schema.sql:82 carries `constraint sairn_audit_checkpoint_one_per_window unique (audit_table, window_end)`, so a retry gets a 23505 rather than a second checkpoint. The schema's own verify step names this exactly -- line 123: "The uniqueness that stops a second run forking the chain exists."
api/audit-checkpoint.js.but: WORTH RECORDING AS A NON-FINDING RATHER THAN SILENCE. This is a hash-chained audit log, so a duplicate checkpoint would put two links where there is one and chain verification would have to decide which is real. The author saw that and constrained it. The checker cannot see a constraint that lives in SQL, which is a scope limit of the checker and not a gap in this file.

api/dnt-bi.js.why: stampUse() is a read-modify-write on a counter -- `use_count: (trow.use_count || 0) + 1` -- so it is the same defect SHAPE as trial-renew.js. THE AUTHOR ALREADY MADE THIS CALL AND WROTE IT DOWN, in the function's own comment: "Read-then-write, so two simultaneous polls can lose a count -- said plainly because use_count is a 'has anyone touched this' signal, not an audited total, and must never be quoted as one."
api/dnt-bi.js.but: RECORDED RATHER THAN RE-DERIVED, which is the point of this entry. The triage's job here is to confirm a judgment already made, not to overturn it -- and to note the condition: the moment use_count is quoted as a total anywhere, this stops being accepted. It is also deliberately not awaited and swallows its own failure, for a stated reason: a dashboard that 500s over a bookkeeping UPDATE.

api/sd-agent.js.why: The POST carries `{model, max_tokens, ...}` to the Claude API. Nothing of ours is written. Same class as api/claude.js and api/sc-eligibility.js.
api/sd-agent.js.but: A retry duplicates a BILLED call and consumes rate-limit budget -- a cost consequence, not a data-integrity one. Third instance of this shape, which is why the checker's scope limit is now recorded against api/_lib/auth.js: any outbound POST reads as a mutating write.

api/sen-portal.js.why: It mints a fresh crypto.randomBytes(32) token per request and inserts a sen_portal_links row. `unique (link_token)` stops the ROW colliding, but a retry mints a NEW token and inserts a SECOND link for the same client. Both work.
api/sen-portal.js.consequence: AN ORPHANED ACCESS CREDENTIAL, which is the opposite of trial-start's failure and worth the contrast: there the caller LOST the token that was minted; here an EXTRA valid one exists. Revoking 'the' link does not revoke the orphan.
api/sen-portal.js.but: Accepted because links are listed and revocable per row, so the orphan is visible rather than hidden. NAMED TRIGGER: if the UI ever shows one link per client rather than a list, the orphan becomes invisible and this entry is wrong. The fix is the same idempotency key trial-start now uses.

api/stonedesk-track.js.why: Identical shape to api/sen-portal.js: a fresh 32-byte token and a new sd_order_links row per request, with a unique index on link_token that stops collision but not duplication. A retry leaves a second working tracking link for the same job.
api/stonedesk-track.js.but: Same conditional as sen-portal, and the two are recorded separately rather than merged for the same reason network.js and org-intel.js are: if the reasoning turns out wrong it is wrong in both, and one merged entry would hide the second.
